annotation.evidence_span: Streams MUST be created or reserved in sequential order, but MAY be used in arbitrary order.
annotation.interpretation_a: Streams must be created/reserved in ascending numerical order, but can be processed/sent out of order.
annotation.interpretation_b: Streams can be created/reserved with gaps in the sequence, but must still be unique and can be used in any order.
annotation.justification: The clause states streams must be created/reserved sequentially, but may be *used* in arbitrary order. This creates ambiguity as to whether the sequential requirement applies to creation/reservation only, or also to usage. If sequential order only applies to creation/reservation, then gaps are allowed, but if it applies to usage as well, then gaps are not allowed.
annotation.missing_information: It is unclear whether 'sequential order' refers to the creation/reservation of StreamIDs or the order in which they are used for data transmission. The meaning of 'reserved' is also unclear; does reserving a StreamID count towards sequential order?
